_doc: Under the Dragon (Tarmac) through the chain (tools/ship_track.sh; ONE-CHAIN section 4 row 6, the rally_stage row: gps, elev, project, mesh, underlay). The draft is the engine's own on County Road 109 (source.type osm: gps fetches the named road from Overpass into data/osm.cache.json -> elev samples USGS 3DEP along it and in a 60 m corridor -> project -> mesh; no widths step: osm_road_widths is off, a graded county road carries no lane count), then the underlay drops data/track.obj into loop.blend as GEN_* collections (scripts/blender/underlay.py). loop false: a POINT-TO-POINT stage (L11) - build_mesh puts the grid 15 m into the road, AC_TIME_0 (the finish) 15 m into the 30 m lead-out past the far end, the two splits at the thirds, and nothing wraps. One layout (stage), so the prep bakes those dummies into the road kn5 (single-layout shape) and no layout_dummies / spawn_kn5 step runs. The prep / exporter run from airoso's scripts/ac, the gates run on the BUILT kn5. The workshop lives OUTSIDE airoso.
_owed: DEPRIORITISED (Kevin 2026-07-26). Chain-ready so the list is complete; the fleet runner may skip it on _deprioritised. Same draft as the gravel twin (same road, same 3DEP) except where road_surface itself forks the engine: build_mesh's fill_apron (tarmac only), the lane paint (road_markings lane + centre yellow), surfaces.ini ROAD friction 0.99, and drive_test holds tarmac to 75 bumps/km and to the paved excursion rule (any >20 cm drop in the verge band, at most 1 per km) where gravel gets 150/km and the unpaved rule - so this track can go red on the gates where its twin is green. Everything owed on the gravel twin is owed here too.
_windows_first: Run --draft-only first (gps needs Overpass, elev needs USGS 3DEP: neither reachable from the container that wrote this). Read, in order: the gps line count and length (expect ~8,400 points / County Road 109 ~25 km; a different length means OSM changed since 2026-07-24); the elev step's '[corridor] sampling' line (data/corridor.elev.json is the near-native 3DEP the mesh splices in; the committed heightfield is the 40 m grid alone); build_mesh's 'terrain_cell_m' / 'corridor] refine' / 'bridge spans' lines; then the full run. The drive_test verdict to read first: floating furniture and severe steps.
